**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                       Date Issued: 20</mark>**<sup>**th**</sup> **<mark>September 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for First Half 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for June 2011 world copper supply and demand in its September 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for June 2011 showed a production deficit of 42,000 metric tonnes (t). However, when making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, June showed a surplus of 32,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first half 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 130,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 100,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 286,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 41,000 t) in the same period of 2010. 

During the first half of 2011, world apparent usage grew by a modest 1% compared with that in the first half of 2010: A growth of apparent usage of 77% in Russia and a 3.5% in the European Union and a 2% growth in reported usage in the United States were partially offset by a decline of 6% in China’s apparent usage*. China’s apparent usage decline in the 1<sup>st</sup> half 2011 reflected a 40% decrease in refined copper net imports from those in the first half of 2010, and the increase in Russia’s apparent usage reflected a 70% decline in net refined exports and commensurate 110% increase in their net exports of semifabricates. Usage in the United States and the EU continued to recover from the recession, although now at a much slower pace than during 2010. On a regional basis, usage grew by 4% in Africa, 2% in the Americas, 10% in Europe, 9% in Oceania, and 2% in Asia ex-China (decline of 3% in Asia incl. China). 

World mine production grew by around 1.5% in the first half of 2011 compared with production in the same half of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 1.4% and solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) by 1.6%. Production at three of the world’s four leading producers (Chile, Peru and the United States), that combined represent one half of the world’s production, was down by an aggregated 2% in the first half of 2011. However, production in China, currently the second leading producer, was up by 15%.  On a regional basis, mine production increased by 2.9% in Africa, 0.3% in the Americas, 3.6% in Europe, and 15% in Oceania, but decreased by around 1% in Asia.  The average mine capacity utilization rate for the first half of 2011 was slightly lower from that in the same period of 2010 at 78%. 

During the first half of 2011, world refined production grew by 2.5% compared with that in the same half of 2010: Primary production increased by 1.3% and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 8%. Production increases of 35% in Australia (recovery from 2010 operational

constraints), 12% in China, and 5% in India were partially offset by declines in Chile (-4%), the United Sates (-8%), Canada (-26%), and Japan (-18%). The average refined capacity utilization rate for the first half of 2011 was unchanged from that in the same period of 2010 at 79%. The average LME cash price for August 2011 was US$9,041.30 per tonne, down from the July 2011 average of US$9,619.24 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of August were US$10,148 and US$8,536.5 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,147.26 per tonne. As of the end of August, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 644,430 t, an increase of 76,248 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010.
